purpose: Olsalazine is used to keep ulcerative colitis under control and prevent flare-ups in people who cannot tolerate another common medication called mesalamine. It helps reduce inflammation in your large intestine (colon). It is mainly used as a maintenance treatment, meaning it helps keep your condition calm rather than treating an active flare.
how_it_works: Olsalazine is made up of two connected molecules that travel through your digestive system mostly unchanged. Once it reaches your colon, friendly bacteria break it apart and release the active ingredient, called mesalamine, right where it is needed. This active ingredient works directly on the lining of your colon to calm down inflammation and reduce irritation.
common_side_effects: Diarrhea is the most common side effect and can affect quite a few people taking this medication. You may also notice stomach cramps, nausea, upset stomach, or heartburn. Some people experience headache, joint aches, or a skin rash. Taking it with food can help reduce stomach-related side effects.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, since this drug can rarely affect these organs over time. Let your doctor know right away if you notice decreased urination, unusual swelling, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or severe stomach pain. People who are allergic to aspirin or salicylates should use caution, as this medication is chemically related. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before starting this medication.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 500 mg (one capsule) taken twice a day, with food, for a total of 1000 mg per day. Always take it with meals to reduce the chance of stomach upset. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on how well you respond and how well you tolerate the medication.
